notes:
Company summary: Proton Stitch Labs builds an in-IDE copilot for enterprise dev teams (VS Code & JetBrains plugins). Primary emphasis: imperceptible completions and inline suggestions — TTFT and jitter are top purchase drivers. They want a predictable streaming experience in the editor and tight token budgets per suggestion so agent + UI remain responsive and cost-controlled.

Requirements (high level):
- Workload: low-latency streaming for completions + few-shot code-edit suggestions; occasional longer refactor generations (batch).
- TTFT target: 30-50ms to first token for warmed paths; cold-start requirement <= 120ms. Client measures TTFT at p50/p95.
- Jitter: aiming for jitter <10ms p95 between first-byte and UI render; p99 <50ms for interactive flows.
- Backpressure: editor must be able to apply backpressure when server-side token backlog > 40 tokens or latency climbs above 120ms — prefer a token-budget-aware pause/resume signal.
- Token budget tuning: default per-suggestion budget 30 tokens for completions, 60 tokens for multi-line suggestions; desire dynamic budgets based on file context and confidence scoring.
- Streaming behavior: chunk size 8-16 tokens; early-stop heuristics to avoid overrun; prefer continuous partial token delivery for UI streaming rather than discrete line-level payloads.
- Model/version pinning: ability to pin to a small quantized model for local latency (e.g., 4-bit Llama-3-8B-like variant) for editor baseline, with automatic fallback to higher-capacity hosted models for longer generations. Version pinning important for reproducible completions across releases.
- Routing/fallback: want policy to route to cheaper quantized variant first and failover to dedicated GPU pool only when prefix KV cache miss or long generations detected.
- Observability: token-level cost & latency breakdown per route, per-model; tooltip for users when model fallback happens.

Technical notes / quotes from SE call: "If TTFT spikes, developers notice immediately — it's the UX dollar. We need <50ms warm-first-byte for single-token completions."

POC scope:
- 14-day Dedicated POC with two configs: (A) low-latency tuned (aggressive pre-warming, small chunk stream, pinned quantized model), (B) cost-optimized (larger batches, relaxed pre-warm).
- Deliverables: TTFT profiler, jitter histogram p50/p95/p99, token-cost per 1k suggestions, backpressure signal integration guide for their VS Code extension.

Next steps / asks from Redwood:
- SE to provide perf harness + recommended runtime flags for pre-warming and KV cache sizing.
- Pricing for Dedicated 3-month pilot and an annual reserved capacity quote.
- Security: provide data residency attestation + SSO SAML steps for sandbox.

Open risks / blockers: SSO cert exchange delayed by customer security team; legal requires explicit residency attestation for EU customers (they plan EU expansion Q3); budget committee approval timeline is gating procurement.
